To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activity of the mitochondrial Complex 1 is reduced in cells with impaired CFTR function.

the activity of mitochondrial Complex I is reduced in cells with impaired CFTR function, either in CF cells, or in non-CF cells treated with inhibitors of CFTR or transfected with CFTR specific shRNAi.

1) the expression of MTND genes is reduced in CF cells, 2) the activity of the mitochondrial Complex-I is reduced in CF and non-CFR cells with impaired CFTR function, 3) the expression of the MTND genes is not affected by the reduction of the activity of the mCxI, and 4) the activity of other mitochondrial complexes is not affected by CFTR inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying mitochondrial dysfunction in CF cells, which could be useful to design new therapeutic strategies to treat CF.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying mitochondrial dysfunctions in CF.
the study of mitochondrial functions in cells with impaired CFTR function.

the CFTR channel is essential to maintain a proper mitochondrial Complex I activity.
mCx-I activity is reduced in cells with impaired CFTR function.
CFTR is involved in the regulation of mCx-I activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CFTR is involved in mitochondrial functions, and the loss of its activity in the CFTR mutated cells may have a role in the development of CF.
the CFTR channel activity regulates the mitochondrial function through the activity of the mCxI.

the mCx-I is a potential therapeutic target for CF and other CFTR-related diseases.
